'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***[[2021 Taliban offensive]]
****The [[Taliban]] tightens its grip in many [[Districts of Afghanistan|districts]] and [[list of cities in Afghanistan|cities]] in northern [[Afghanistan]] as [[President of Afghanistan|Afghan President]] [[Ashraf Ghani]] calls on local militias to fight the armed group. [[The Pentagon|Pentagon]] spokesman [[John Kirby (admiral)|John Kirby]] says that the [[United States]] is willing to continue their [[airstrike]] campaign against the Taliban but warned that "it is up to the Afghan government to defend themselves" and also added that "it is their struggle". [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/taliban-tighten-control-afghan-north-residents-weigh-options-2021-08-10/ (Reuters)]
****Afghan President Ashraf Ghani says he views peace talks with the Taliban as concluded and unsuccessful, and anticipates a civil war. [https://www.stripes.com/theaters/middle_east/2021-08-10/afghanistan-taliban-peace-talks-dead-ashraf-ghani-2513250.html?fbclid=IwAR1hzZ1zs4YNJjzOseS2W2N1G5lYjGS-B_H8Hlz2jZWZLEe1zdDx2aU3Zek (''Stars and Stripes'')]
****The Taliban captures the city of [[Farah, Afghanistan|Farah]], the capital of the southwestern [[Farah Province]], as well as the city of [[Puli Khumri]], the capital of the northern [[Baghlan Province]]. These are the seventh and eighth provincial capitals to fall under Taliban control in the past five days. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/10/taliban-seizes-farah-seventh-provincial-afghan-capital-in-five-days (Al Jazeera)]
**[[2007 Bagram Airfield bombing]]
***A report published from the [[Afghanistan Papers]] by ''[[The Washington Post]]'' journalist [[Craig Whitlock]] accuses former [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[George W. Bush]] and [[Presidency of George W. Bush|his administration]] of lying about the Taliban attempting to kill former [[Vice President of the United States|U.S. Vice President]] [[Dick Cheney]] during a [[2007 Bagram Airfield bombing|2007 attack]] on the [[Bagram Airfield]] base. [https://www.thedailybeast.com/bush-administration-lied-about-taliban-nearly-killing-cheney-in-2007-suicide-attack-says-report (''The Daily Beast'')]
*[[Tigray War]]
**[[Ethiopia|Ethiopian]] [[Prime Minister of Ethiopia|Prime Minister]] [[Abiy Ahmed]] calls on "all eligible citizens" to join the [[Ethiopian National Defense Force|armed forces]] to "stop the Tigray forces once and for all" and for all Ethiopians to "show patriotism" in this moment. Abiy had promised a swift victory when the war broke out in late 2020, but this changed in June when Tigrayan forces recaptured the [[Tigray Region|region]] and advanced further into other regions. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/10/ethiopia-calls-on-civilians-to-join-army-to-fight-tigray-rebels (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Algeria wildfires]]
**[[Wildfire]]s continue in [[Tizi Ouzou Province]], [[Algeria]], killing 25 soldiers during rescue operations and 10 more civilians, bringing the death toll to 42. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/11/wildfires-algeria-soldiers-climate (Al Jazeera)]
*International seafood company [[Grieg Seafood]] announces that it has accidentally dumped 4,000 gallons of [[chlorine]] in a [[Norway|Norwegian]] [[fjord]], killing approx. 96,000 fish. The company apologizes and says it will handle the cleanup. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/96000-fish-killed-chlorine-leak-grieg-seafood-norway/ (CBS News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] begins to [[vaccine|vaccinate]] [[Rohingya]] refugees in 34 camps in [[Cox's Bazar]] district which borders [[Myanmar]] as the increase in the number of [[COVID-19]] cases poses health risks in the camps where more than one million refugees are living. [https://apnews.com/article/health-bangladesh-coronavirus-pandemic-united-nations-2fc02f9b29fb6544e4a115d70f5fdab8 (Associated Press)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in East Timor]]
****[[East Timor]] reports its first community transmitted cases of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant]] in 12 samples from the [[Ermera]] region. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-08-10/east-timor-detects-first-domestic-transmission-of-covid-19-delta-variant?context=amp (U.S. News & World Report)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] eases its COVID-19-related restrictions for people who have been fully [[COVID-19 vaccination in Malaysia|vaccinated]] against COVID-19 in eight [[States of Malaysia|state]]s where the number of cases have been declined that allow people to cross-border travel, play individual outdoor sports, and eat at restaurants. The [[Government of Malaysia|government]] also eases the 14-day home [[quarantine]] for fully vaccinated people and allow married couple to cross state borders to meet their spouses regardless of their state. [https://www.thejakartapost.com/seasia/2021/08/09/malaysia-to-ease-covid-19-restrictions-for-fully-vaccinated-in-eight-states-.html (''The Jakarta Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
****[[Singapore]] begins to ease some [[social distancing]] measures and allows indoor dining to resume at food and beverage establishments and increases the maximum group size to five people for those who have been fully [[COVID-19 vaccination in Singapore|vaccinated]] or who have recovered from COVID-19. However, unvaccinated people are only allowed to dine in groups of up to two people at coffee shops and [[hawker centre]]s. [https://www.todayonline.com/singapore/covid-19-moh-spells-out-eligibility-criteria-dining-fb-outlets-hard-copies-overseas (''Today'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record 235 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|death]]s from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 6,588. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2163027/record-235-new-covid-fatalities-19-843-new-cases (''Bangkok Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] and leaders of 16 [[Germany|German]] [[States of Germany|state]]s agree to phase out free [[COVID-19 testing]] for citizens beginning on October 11 and will begin requiring non-vaccinated people to show a negative test result to enter certain indoor venues as well as to attend cultural, sport, and entertainment events once the infection rate in a region reaches 35 per 100,000 people unless they have recovered from COVID-19 in order to pressure people to get [[COVID-19 vaccination in Germany|vaccinated]]. [https://amp.theguardian.com/world/2021/aug/10/germany-to-abolish-free-covid-testing-in-bid-to-get-more-people-vaccinated (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports 146 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total of deaths since March 12. [https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-uk-records-23-510-new-coronavirus-cases-and-146-more-deaths-daily-figures-show-12378094 (Sky News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
***[[Fiji]] surpasses 300 deaths from COVID-19. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/448842/covid-19-in-fiji-18-more-deaths-603-new-cases-confirmed (RNZ International)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Martinique]]
***The [[French overseas department]] of [[Martinique]] enters a three-week strict [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] that closes all non-essential shops as well as hotels and [[culture|cultural]] and leisure venues such as beaches in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19. Residents must also restrict their movement to within {{cvt|1|km}} from their homes. [https://amp.rfi.fr/en/france/20210810-martinique-goes-into-strict-lockdown-tourists-encouraged-to-leave-caribbean-covid-19 (Radio France Internationale)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***The U.S. surpasses 36 million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.kiro7.com/news/trending/coronavirus-total-us-covid-19-cases-top-36-million-death-toll-nears-618000/KHSTP64YLNF55M5234CENKXLKI/ (KIRO-TV)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Capital punishment in China]]
**A court in [[China]] upholds the [[death sentence]] of a [[Canadians|Canadian]] man convicted of [[drug smuggling]]. The man, originally sentenced to 15 years imprisonment, had his sentence upgraded on appeal. [[Canadian authorities]] say that the sentence is in retaliation for the arrest of [[Meng Wanzhou]], the [[CFO]] of [[Huawei]], in [[Vancouver]] in 2018. [https://www.dw.com/en/china-court-rejects-canadian-mans-appeal-against-death-sentence/a-58813556 (Deutsche Welle)]
*[[Government of Russia|Russian authorities]] open a criminal investigation into [[Leonid Volkov (politician)|Leonid Volkov]] and [[Ivan Zhdanov]], two prominent allies of incarcerated activist [[Alexei Navalny]], for raising funds for a banned political network. It is the first investigation of its kind on Navalny's allies. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/close-ally-kremlin-critic-navalny-leaves-russia-amid-crackdown-rt-ren-tv-cite-2021-08-08/ (Reuters)]
*[[Voting rights in the United States]]
**[[Texas]] [[Speaker of the Texas House of Representatives|House Speaker]] [[Dade Phelan]] signs 52 arrest warrants for [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] lawmakers who broke quorum to stop the passing of legislation that would limit voting access for some citizens. [https://www.ksat.com/news/texas/2021/08/10/texas-house-orders-arrest-of-missing-democrats-as-weekslong-stalemate-over-a-voting-restrictions-bill-continues/?fbclid=IwAR22vzOFlPLtz2dy9DcIIF4dOo8tzK7iG4Sl_gi1NA0Oykum33U7ElVHprs (KSAT-TV)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Andrew Cuomo sexual harassment allegations]]
**[[Andrew Cuomo]] announces his resignation as [[Governor of New York]] following allegations of sexual harassment, as well as an investigatory report by [[New York Attorney General]] [[Letitia James]] which stated that Cuomo sexually harassed 11 women during his time in office. Cuomo's resignation will take effect on August 24 and he will be succeeded by [[Lieutenant Governor of New York|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Kathy Hochul]], who will become the first woman to serve as Governor of New York. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/politics-news/new-york-gov-andrew-cuomo-resigns-n1260310/ (NBC News)]
*The [[Poland|Polish]] coalition government collapses after [[Prime Minister of Poland|Prime Minister]] [[Mateusz Morawiecki]] dismissed [[Deputy Prime Minister of Poland|deputy prime minister]] [[Jarosław Gowin]], who is leading the governing party partner [[Agreement (political party)|Agreement]] motivated by disagreements with fiscal policy and a controversial media law. [https://www.politico.eu/article/poland-ruling-coalition-collapses-media-law-protests/ (''Politico Europe'')]
*The U.S. [[United States Senate|Senate]] passes a bipartisan [[United States dollar|$]]1 [[Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act|trillion infrastructure bill]], featuring provisions for broadband access, clean water, electric grid renewal, transportation and road proposals. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-senate-poised-pass-1-trillion-infrastructure-bill-debate-35-trillion-budget-2021-08-10/?fbclid=IwAR0t6f4k02cWosfTcAVtdsTQ1R7WX-F1JkUftwnmrLwOewrSrUqXHOAnZNQ (Reuters)]
